Summary.Title: Universal Assurance Kernel Schema
Summary.KernelAuthorityBoundary: The Universal Assurance Kernel defines shared assurance primitives and validation rules. It has no independent approval, release, override, execution, or source-of-truth authority.
Summary.HumanAuthorityRule: Qualified humans and authorized organizational roles remain responsible for binding decisions.
Summary.SourceOfTruthRule: Official records remain in governed source systems.
Summary.Step153Statement: Step 153 defines a universal schema baseline. It does not implement runtime services, modify existing architecture, validate production systems, certify controls, or authorize regulated execution.
Summary.Step154Gate: READY AFTER STEP 153 UNIVERSAL ASSURANCE KERNEL REVIEW

Invariants.Rule: Official records remain in governed source systems. The kernel does not replace the official record.
Qualified humans and authorized organizational roles remain accountable for binding decisions.
Evidence cannot support an assurance decision unless origin, object linkage, time, and source are known.
Integrity seals must identify the algorithm and evidence scope and must support later rehash verification.
Missed alerts, absent objection, unavailable approvers, and silent dashboards must not create authority.
A workflow is not trustworthy when required dependencies, evidence, identity, controls, reviews, and source states disagree.
Thread D, Thread D2, RAMAT Vision, glasses, wearables, dashboards, and device witnesses may display state but may not decide or execute.
Missing, unresolved, delayed, conflicting, and unknown states must be explicit and must not be treated as satisfied.
An admissibility record evaluates whether an action may proceed; it does not itself execute the action.
Platform B v1 and Thread D v1 remain architecture locked. The kernel does not reopen either architecture.
